full_judgment: 5. In the instant case, the plaintiff petitioners challenged the kabalas Exhibitsl and 1(ka) as products of forgery and false personation by Salamatullah, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants. The onus of proof of forgery and false personation is on the plaintiffs who allege that the documents are forged and fabricated. The original kabalas were not produced. Certified copies of those two impugned kabalas were produced by both the parties which were marked as Exhibits 1 and 1(Ka) by the trial court. The trial court accepted those documents and admitted them into evidence. From the evidence on record it has transpired that Charag Ali, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs was not only an educated and well-known person in the locality but also a close relation of the Sub-Registrar. It is also on evidence that Charag Ali executed and registered two documents in the year 1918 and 1950 wherein the endorsement is simply that the executant Charag Ali is personally known to me (the Sub-registrar) and there is no endorsement that he was exempted from putting his thumb impression. This fact was admitted by PW 1 Luful Karim son of Charag Ali when he was confronted with those kabalas. When the plaintiffs assert that the impugned kabalas were forged by impersonation it was the duty of the plaintiffs to take steps to prove that the thumb impressions as contained in the impugned documents were not of Charag Ali but of Salamat Ullah. It is on record that two registered kabalas, being Kabala Nos. 584 and 585 dated 26-2-1918 exempted by Charag Ali were on record about which PW 1 Lutful Karim son of the executant Charag Ali admitted that his father by those two kabalas sold out lands in 1918. In those kabalas Charag Ali was not exempted from putting his LTI and in those Kabalas also there were no endorsements of the Sub-Registrar exempting Charag Ali from putting his left thumb impression. If the plaintiffs were serious and wanted to prove the forgery by impersonation then the LTI's of Charag Ali in thumb impression and signature book could have been called for by them and compared with the two kabalas of 1918. Thus, for non-production of the original kabalas it cannot be said that the plaintiffs did not get any opportunity to compare the LTI's of Charag Ali as the two kabalas of 26-2-1918 were on record. The plaintiffs did not take any effective steps to discharge the onus of proof that the impugned kabalas were forged by impersonation. It may be mentioned that the kabalas having been admittedly registered on 11-7-47 there is a presumption of correctness attached to the documents themselves that the registration was done validly and legally. Admittedly, the documents are old documents of 50 years back and there is no evidence that the defendants willfully suppressed the said documents from production in court. The broad fact remains that the trial court also accepted the certified copies of the kabalas.
